scope: Source-only followup; no ioctl, tracing, native run, build or dependency adoption.

findings.i915_gem_throttle.c: Enumerates currently registered contexts and their engine timelines; selects an incomplete request older than20ms and waits for request completion. Recent requests are skipped. No demonstrated wait for previously removed contexts to transfer runtime into client past_runtime. Not a finalization barrier.
findings.i915_gem_wait.c: Object reservation fences are waited through i915_request_wait_timeout or dma_fence_wait_timeout. Already-signaled fences may return immediately. Wait reservation calls the boost prescan, which can invoke intel_rps_boost for requests not started. Neither the ioctl nor its inspected object-wait path establishes the required context accounting transfer postcondition.

inference: These APIs cannot supply the missing proof for the existing retained-fd draft. This does not establish that every runtime read loses counts or that no complete DRM method exists.
next_requirement: Find an observable accounting-retirement completion mechanism covering explicit context replacement/destruction, with exact deployed-driver identity, client lifetime coverage, loss semantics and overhead. A kernel accounting/event approach remains unselected and would need its own privilege/coverage proposal; no execution authority.
qualification: Complete duty remains unavailable. Painter-hover correction awaits separate owner approval; no relation between this source followup and renderer execution authority.
limitations: Inspected upstream v6.12.107 remains a pinned feasibility source, not proof of exact installed Debian build or active backend equivalence.
